full_text_en:
Zhao Ziwen v. Pan Riyang — dispute over property infringement

Ruling Summary

The phrase "the domicile of one party is not within this jurisdiction" as used in the Notice of the Supreme People's Court on Adjusting the Standards for the Jurisdiction of High People's Courts and Intermediate People's Courts over First Instance Civil and Commercial Cases refers to the situation where only one of the plaintiff or the defendant has its domicile outside the jurisdiction, and does not include the situation where the domiciles of both the plaintiff and the defendant are outside the jurisdiction. In a joint action, if the domicile of one of the plaintiffs or one of the defendants is outside the jurisdiction, this falls within the situation referred to as "the domicile of one party is not within this jurisdiction" in the above-mentioned notice. Since a third party participates in the litigation between others, regardless of whether it is a third party with an independent claim or a third party without an independent claim, whether its domicile is within this jurisdiction does not affect the jurisdiction over the case.

Civil Ruling of the Supreme People's Court

(2010) Min Yi Zhong Zi No. 17

Appellant (Defendant at First Instance): Pan Riyang, male, Han ethnicity, born on October 27, 1956, residing at Room 302, Unit 1, Building 18, Huihao Tianxia, Dongshangyi Street, Yuquan District, Hohhot City, Inner Mongolia Autonomous Region.

Appellee (Plaintiff at First Instance): Zhao Ziwen, male, Han ethnicity, born on January 12, 1961, residing at Unit 14, Unit 3, Building 85, Zhenhua Street, Datong City, Shanxi Province.

Appellant Pan Riyang, in the dispute over property infringement with Appellee Zhao Ziwen, appealed against the Civil Ruling (2009) Shan Min Yi Chu Zi No. 2 of the Shaanxi High People's Court to this Court. This Court lawfully formed a collegial panel to hear this case. The case is now concluded.

The court of first instance held that the amount in dispute in this case was RMB 50 million, and the domiciles of both parties were not within the Shaanxi region. Whether this case fell within the jurisdiction of that court as a first instance civil or commercial case was the focal point of the dispute between the parties. According to Article 1, Paragraph 2 of the Notice of the Supreme People's Court on Adjusting the Standards for the Jurisdiction of High People's Courts and Intermediate People's Courts over First Instance Civil and Commercial Cases (Fa Fa [2008] No. 10), that court could have jurisdiction over first instance civil and commercial cases with an amount in dispute of RMB 100 million or more, as well as first instance civil and commercial cases with an amount in dispute of RMB 50 million or more where the domicile of one party was not within the jurisdiction, or which involved foreign, Hong Kong, Macao, or Taiwan elements. The second case jurisdiction standard in that provision both excluded possible local protection factors and, to a certain extent, reduced the litigation costs of the parties, reflecting judicial fairness. However, the phrase "and the domicile of one party is not within this jurisdiction" in that provision could not be simply interpreted as only the situation where one party is outside the jurisdiction, because the provision did not exclude the situation where both parties are outside the jurisdiction. Hearing civil or commercial cases with an amount in dispute of RMB 50 million or more where the domiciles of both parties are outside the jurisdiction by that court was more conducive to getting rid of the influence of local protectionism. Additionally, Zhao Ziwen had previously sued Pan Riyang in that court in the name of a legal person regarding the same legal facts, and that court had previously heard the case. Considering the actual circumstances of this case, having that court hear it was more conducive to ascertaining the facts of the case, improving judicial efficiency, lawfully protecting the legitimate rights and interests of both parties, and achieving judicial fairness. In summary, Pan Riyang's jurisdictional objection requesting the transfer of the case to the Yulin Intermediate People's Court was not sustainable. Pursuant to Article 38 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, it was ruled to reject Pan Riyang's objection to the jurisdiction of this case.

Pan Riyang, dissatisfied with the first instance ruling, appealed to this Court, arguing: The first instance ruling's interpretation of the Notice of the Supreme People's Court on Adjusting the Standards for the Jurisdiction of High People's Courts and Intermediate People's Courts over First Instance Civil and Commercial Cases (Fa Fa [2008] No. 10) did not conform to the original legislative intent. The meaning of "an amount in dispute of RMB 50 million or more and the domicile of one party is not within this jurisdiction" should be that the domicile of one party is not within the jurisdiction while the domicile of the other party is within the jurisdiction, and does not include the situation where the domiciles of both parties are outside the jurisdiction. Therefore, he requested this Court to lawfully revoke the first instance ruling and rule that this case be heard by the Yulin Intermediate People's Court of Shaanxi Province.

Zhao Ziwen did not submit a written defense.

This Court holds that this case is an appeal filed by a party dissatisfied with a ruling of a High People's Court on an objection to subject matter jurisdiction. According to Article 8 of the Provisions of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues Concerning the Trial of Cases of Objection to Subject Matter Jurisdiction, this Court shall lawfully hear the case and render a ruling. The phrase "the domicile of one party is not within this jurisdiction" as used in the Notice of the Supreme People's Court on Adjusting the Standards for the Jurisdiction of High People's Courts and Intermediate People's Courts over First Instance Civil and Commercial Cases (Fa Fa [2008] No. 10) refers to the situation where the domicile of either the plaintiff or the defendant is not within the jurisdiction, and does not include the situation where the domiciles of both the plaintiff and the defendant are outside the jurisdiction. Where the domiciles of both the plaintiff and the defendant are outside the jurisdiction, the subject matter jurisdiction court shall be determined solely based on the standard of the amount in dispute. In the case of a joint action, where the domicile of one of the plaintiffs or one of the defendants is outside the jurisdiction, it shall be considered a situation of "the domicile of one party is not within this jurisdiction." Regarding a third party whose domicile is outside the jurisdiction, whether it is a third party with an independent claim or a third party without an independent claim, since it participates in the litigation between others, based on a balancing of the jurisdictional interests of the plaintiff and defendant, it should not be classified as a situation of "the domicile of one party is not within this jurisdiction." The amount in dispute in this case is RMB 50 million or more, but the domiciles of both parties are outside the jurisdiction. According to Article 1 of the Provisions of the Supreme People's Court on Several Issues Concerning the Trial of Cases of Objection to Subject Matter Jurisdiction, the Shaanxi High People's Court has no jurisdiction over this case and should transfer it to a people's court with jurisdiction for trial. Since the alleged infringing act occurred in Shenmu County, Shaanxi Province, the Shaanxi High People's Court should transfer this case to the Yulin Intermediate People's Court of Shaanxi Province for trial.

In conclusion, the first instance ruling was erroneous in holding that the Shaanxi High People's Court had jurisdiction over this case and should be corrected. The appellant's appeal request to revoke the first instance ruling and transfer this case to the Yulin Intermediate People's Court of Shaanxi Province for trial is well-founded and should be supported. Pursuant to Article 38, Article 153, Paragraph 1, Item (2), and Article 154 of the Civil Procedure Law of the People's Republic of China, it is ruled as follows:

1. Revoke the Civil Ruling (2009) Shan Min Yi Chu Zi No. 2 of the Shaanxi High People's Court;

2. The Shaanxi High People's Court shall transfer this case to the Yulin Intermediate People's Court of Shaanxi Province for trial.

This ruling is final.

Presiding Judge: Jiang Qibo
Acting Judge: Wang Shengquan
Acting Judge: Li Yanchen

March 24, 2010

Clerk: Shao Haiqiang

[Introduction to the Presiding Judge]

Jiang Qibo, Senior Judge: Born in 1963, Doctor of Laws, served as Deputy Chief Judge of the Case Filing Division of the Supreme People's Court from 2005, and served as Deputy Chief Judge of the First Case Filing Division of the Supreme People's Court from 2009.
